answer: Yes. Annual salary increases are in place for every step of every salary schedule. Movement from step 9 to step 10a and then to step 10b follows the previous contract's manner, requiring a teacher to remain at step 10a for six months of the work-year before moving to step 10b, with any remaining months from the prior contract carried over into the new contract. Teachers who receive an unsatisfactory rating are not eligible to advance to the next step in the subsequent school year. On the Career Ladder salary schedule, Advanced Study and Longevity do not apply. For the VIEW Pay Program pilot, teachers at the top of the salary schedule relinquish the negotiated increment (with 40% of the bonus rolling to base salary annually), while tenured teachers on internal steps continue step advancement.

answer: Yes. The document includes the VIEW (Voluntary Incentive Earnings at Work) Pay Program, a voluntary pilot program for current teachers in positions requiring certification. Eligible teachers may volunteer, and the bonus ranges up to a maximum of $8,000 per volunteer annually. To participate, teachers must demonstrate the ability to grow student achievement, using value-added measures for core subjects or Student Learning Outcomes designated by a design team for non-core subjects. If more than the maximum number of teachers volunteer, a random selection will take place. For top-step teachers, 40% of the bonus will roll to the base salary schedule annually, while tenured teachers on internal steps will see no portion roll to their salary step. At the conclusion of the pilot, participants may choose to continue or return to the traditional salary schedule, though those entering the successor plan cannot opt out. Pilot participation caps increase annually: 75 teachers in 2011-2012, 125 in 2012-2013, 175 in 2013-2014, and 225 in 2014-2015.

answer: Teachers must demonstrate the ability to grow student achievement. For core subjects, a value-added model of calculating student achievement is used; for teachers without such testing data, Student Learning Outcomes are designated by a design team of fourteen teachers and two administrators (defined as explicit statements describing knowledge, skills, abilities, and attitudes a student will demonstrate). For Career Ladder advancement, teachers must achieve an acceptable student growth standard and either attain desired performance levels on effective teaching practice components evaluated collaboratively by trained teachers and administrators, or rank in the top 20% of their cohort based on student growth. For PRC cohort bonus eligibility, evaluation uses value-added modeling (VAM) based on better-than-expected results in student academic achievement, attendance, and course credits earned. For Enrichment Period (EP) teacher selection, interim criteria consist of an application, an interview, and a portfolio review.

answer: Yes. The document provides annual Career Ladder differentials for teachers in high-need roles: $13,300 for Clinical Resident Instructors (207 workdays/eight hour day), $12,200 for Turnaround Teachers (deployed to low-performing classrooms in K-5, K-8, and middle schools for 3-year terms/198 workdays/eight hour day), $11,300 for Instructional Teacher Leaders (202 workdays/eight hour day), $9,300 for Learning Environment Specialists (197 workdays/eight hour day), and $9,300 for Promise Readiness Corps (197 workdays/eight hour day, 2-year term). The PRC cohort bonus is based on value-added modeling (VAM) of a team's contribution over the two-year cycle, rewarding better-than-expected results in academic achievement, attendance, and course credits. Eligibility for the bonus requires a minimum 60% assignment to the role (or 50% with an exceptional schedule), and any teacher receiving an unsatisfactory rating is ineligible for the bonus and must leave the PRC team. Non-Career Ladder PRC teachers and support staff (counselors and social workers) are ineligible for the differential, though support staff may receive the cohort bonus.

Right of return is not applicable, and voluntary transfers during the term will not be honored. Turnaround Teachers are deployed as cultural change agents in low-performing classrooms for 3-year assignments in K-5, K-8, and middle schools, with a normal four-member team filling three teaching positions; they are relieved from duty for planning time and serve on school leadership teams. CRIs work 15 additional days annually (scheduled by March 1 of the preceding year) and teach a reduced course-load as mentors/coaches. PRC teams consist of 6-8 teachers linked to 100-120 students, looping from 9th to 10th grade, with a maximum of 20 students per teacher and meetings at least twice per week. To earn the PRC differential, a teacher's assignment must be at least 60% (or 50% if exceptional schedule). Evaluation is linked to a fifth domain of the RISE Rubric, requiring a preponderance of proficient and distinguished performance to continue; an unsatisfactory rating blocks continuation and cohort bonus. Level advancement requires an acceptable student growth standard, allows only one level advance per decision point, and for experienced hires requires three years of student growth measures with no advancements prior to the 2014-15 school year. Advanced Study and Longevity do not apply to the Career Ladder salary schedule.
